paper_metadata.title: Effect of Zr micro-alloying on microstructure refinement and mechanical property of CoCrNi medium-entropy alloy processed by high-pressure torsion and subsequent annealing

The as-cast materials were cold-rolled with 80% reduction in thickness and subsequently homogenized at 1100 °C for 24 h in a vacuum (~ 10–3 Pa) furnace.

mechanisms.name: grain refinement strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: HPT-deformed and annealed at 900 °C for 1 h

evidence.quote: First, the Zr addition increased the strength by refining the grain size of the FCC matrix.

mechanisms.name: precipitation strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: HPT-deformed and annealed at 800 °C for 10 min

evidence.quote: The second impact of Zr on mechanical properties resulted from precipitation hardening.

mechanisms.name: dislocation locking by Zr segregation at dislocation sites

evidence.quote: The strength enhancement was due to grain refinement, precipitation, and dislocation locking caused by the Zr segregation at dislocation sites.
This suggests that the growth kinetics of precipitates were relatively slow, which makes these precipitates effective in hindering the grain growth in the FCC matrix.

mechanisms.name: dislocation looping (by-pass) around precipitates
mechanisms.material_state: HPT-deformed and annealed at 800 °C for 10 min

evidence.quote: we assume that the by-pass (dislocation looping) mechanism [35] is the dominant interaction between dislocations and precipitates.
